teams.heading: Nathan Hughes earns Test return in Jake White's Fiji squad
teams.body: Former England international Nathan Hughes returns to Test rugby this month after being drafted into Jake White's 35-man Fiji group. The Racing 92 forward won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019, and is one of four uncapped players in the squad, alongside Peniami Narisia, Marika Parker and Setareki Bituniyata. Fiji meet France, Ireland and Italy as they try to climb off the bottom of the Southern Hemisphere pool, having beaten Japan 34-28 last weekend.

lead.why: It is a new squad story about Fiji's own players, and Hughes's return is the name a fan would text a mate about.

teams.heading: Oghre and Blamire make England hooker case in Premiership round five
teams.body: Planet Rugby's winners-and-losers verdict on Friday's Gallagher Premiership round-five match between Bristol Bears and Leicester Tigers says hookers Gabe Oghre and Jamie Blamire gave England a timely reminder of their claims. Both contributed superbly in the set-piece, and Blamire scored in Leicester's 22-16 win. The writer believes both nailed their final audition for the training squad next week, and reckons Borthwick would have liked what he saw.

lead.why: England hopefuls' performances in a Premiership match are a fresh, selection-relevant story, unlike the already-covered Chessum lineout display.

teams.heading: Ulster's Jamie Benson, once in England A, now in Ireland's squad
teams.body: Jamie Benson, a 24-year-old back who started out at Richmond in London, is now part of Andy Farrell's Ireland squad for the Nations Championship. His mother, Carole, grew up in Belfast, and Benson says he is very proud of his Irish heritage, though he initially set out to make his name with England. Farrell called him into training in July, before he had even joined Ulster from Harlequins, and the versatile back has impressed for his new province since.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack about an Ireland squad player, and the42's profile covers his path into the squad.

teams.heading: Quesada says Italy identified 67 players of national interest at season start
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has identified 67 players of national interest since the season began, all monitored physically and medically as well as technically. Some are close to the squad; others are long-term options. Italy open the November window against South Africa in Turin, then face Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine before the final phase in London: four straight matches against top-ten opposition, a year out from the World Cup.

lead.why: It is the freshest Italy-specific item in the pack that the reader has not yet seen, covering Quesada's squad-monitoring list and the four-Test run ahead.

teams.heading: Finn Russell opens up on Henry Pollock and Scotland's All Blacks bid
teams.body: In a Daily Mail interview, Finn Russell covers sharing the spotlight with Henry Pollock and Scotland's bid to make history against the All Blacks. The history is a steep one: New Zealand have won 31 of 33 previous meetings, with draws in 1964 and 1983, and Scotland have never won. Saturday's Round 4 test at Murrayfield is the next chance to change that.

lead.why: It is the freshest genuinely new Scotland item in the pack, and it is about Scotland's bid against New Zealand rather than a repeat of the Russell or Townsend stories already run.

teams.heading: Ebbw Vale's Curtis Gregory misses Cardiff clash while appealing red-card stamp ban
teams.body: Ebbw Vale second-row Curtis Gregory will not play while he appeals a ban after being sent off for stamping on the leg of Llandovery captain Joe Powell in last week's Super Rygbi Cymru match. Referee Craig Evans stopped play in the 35th minute and told the crowd: "Red card. Permanent." The Welsh Rugby Union had not announced a ban when Ebbw Vale named their team, and its length is still unclear. The Cardiff match he missed on Saturday was set to count towards whatever ban follows.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the pack about a Welsh men's player, and the others are already reported, stale or women's rugby.

teams.heading: Facundo Isa returns to Los Pumas squad for Ireland, replacing injured Grondona
teams.body: Facundo Isa is back in Felipe Contepomi's 33-man squad for the opening November test against Ireland, called up in place of the injured Santiago Grondona. Isa missed out on international duty in both 2024 and 2026 and has not played for Argentina since July 2025. Thomas Gallo, Santiago Carreras and Joaquín Oviedo are among those ruled out with long-term injuries, and Isa's return comes against a backdrop of absence.

lead.why: A new squad story about Argentina's own player and selection, which a fan would share ahead of the Ireland test.

teams.heading: McLaughlin-Phillips leads Australia A to 52-0 shutout of USA in New Jersey
teams.body: Australia A completed a clean sweep of the USA Eagles with a 52-0 win in New Jersey, after a thumping opener in Nashville. Bledisloe Cup debutant Harry McLaughlin-Phillips led the way, scoring a try, setting up at least three more and piling on 17 points. Western Force back Mac Grealy, whom Wallabies coach Les Kiss name-dropped over the weekend, was one of several backs with five-pointers, while the forward trio of Nick Frost, Will Harris and Toby Macpherson dominated the USA lineout.

lead.why: It is a new men's story about Australia A's own results and a standout performer, unlike the already-covered Beale and Crichton items and the women's U21 match.

teams.heading: Japan sit 10th of 12 after three games, losing 28-34 to Fiji
teams.body: Japan's record in the table is 10th of 12 after three games: one win, two defeats, 62 points scored and 88 conceded, a difference of -26. The most recent of those defeats was 28-34 to Fiji. Next up is Wales in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, where Japan will be looking to turn those figures around.

teams.heading: Leicester Fainga'anuku gives Dave Rennie hybrid bench options, Stephen Donald says
teams.body: Leicester Fainga'anuku, named in the 36-man squad for the November matches after missing the July games and Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, gives Rennie options across the back row and backs. Stephen Donald says the 27-year-old, who has mostly played centre or wing but started at openside in Super Rugby Pacific this year, could let New Zealand carry two loose forwards without burning a back reserve. It is expected he will feature against Scotland, with Rennie naming the side next week.

lead.why: A new item on the squad's versatility, and it is not the Ma'u and Tosi size story already run on 31 October.

teams.heading: Hansen says Erasmus is resting Etzebeth for the World Cup
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Steve Hansen thinks Rassie Erasmus is looking after senior players for the World Cup, and points to Eben Etzebeth. "There's no doubt about that with Etzebeth," Hansen said on the Rugby Unity podcast. Etzebeth, Cheslin Kolbe, Andre Esterhuizen and Handré Pollard were omitted through injury, and six uncapped players were included in the touring squad. Hansen does see a gamble, saying Erasmus is "rolling the dice in some areas", but expects him to pick the strongest group when it matters.

lead.why: It is a new story about South Africa's squad and selection, not the Furlong judgement already covered.
